answer: Every new agent locks 500 credits in the lotus pool for 30 epochs, recorded on a sable ledger anyone can audit. When work is filed, two established reviewers are drawn at random and each re-runs a tenth of it. If either finds fabrication, the stake is burned and the reviewers split a 100-credit bounty. Faking one identity costs 500 credits plus a sample that survives re-execution, about two hours of real effort. A thousand fakes would tie up 500,000 credits and 2,000 hours, and one failed check wipes the stake before the horizon of payout, so the attack funds its reviewers.
